picks.title: Yom Kippur: Appreciating and Achieving Greatness
picks.summary:
You put on tefillin. You hold back one piece of lashon hara. You say one tefillah with real kavana. It can feel like such a small thing. But what if the true impact of that mitzvah is far greater than anything you can see? Rabbi Shafier reveals a fascinating picture of how your choices affect not only yourself, but the spiritual worlds beyond you. Discover why even the smallest mitzvah matters more than you realize, why an aveirah carries such weight, and how understanding the true power of your actions can completely change the way you approach Yom Kippur.

picks.reason: Rabbi Shafier reveals deep spiritual impact of mitzvot and ethical choices.

picks.title: The Shmuz on the Parsha: Ha'azinu
picks.summary:
Is there anything you've done that is simply too big to undo? Any mistake that puts you beyond the reach of teshuvah? In this powerful shmuz, Rabbi Shafier explores the extraordinary story of Elisha ben Avuyah, a man who rose to incredible spiritual heights and then fell almost as far as a person could fall. Yet even for him, the door to teshuvah was never truly closed. Discover the mistake that kept Acher from returning, the astonishing power of teshuvah, and why no matter how far you've fallen, it's never too late to come back. 
 This podcast has been graciously sponsored by JewishPodcasts.f
picks.reason: Explores teshuvah and spiritual fall in a classic Jewish story of Elisha ben Avuyah.

picks.title: Yom Kippur - The 955th Gate
picks.summary: What happens when it feels like the door has closed?Acher hears a Bas Kol say, “Return, wayward children, except for Acher.” Neilah itself is the moment when the gates are closing.And yet Chazal teach us that this is precisely the moment not to give up.In this dhmoy, delivered at Mevaseret Mishmar, Rav Burg explores one of the deepest ideas in teshuvah: that even when everything seems sealed, even when a person feels too far gone, there is still a place beyond despair. Teshuvah reaches all the way to the Kisei HaKavod.Sometimes the gate that seems to be closing is the gate you are meant to kee

picks.showTitle: Search for Meaning with Rabbi Yoshi
picks.title: Hineini: Showing Up and Staying Human in the Age of AI
picks.summary: Rosh Hashanah morning at Stephen Wise Temple, Rabbi Yoshi Zweiback explores an ancient Hebrew word — Hineini, "Here I am" — through the lens of one of the newest challenges facing us: artificial intelligence. Weaving together the Binding of Isaac, a teaching from the Mussar master Rabbi Eliyahu Lopian, and the work of Israeli thinker Micah Goodman, Rabbi Zweiback asks what AI can and cannot give us — and what it means to keep practicing the very human capacities technology can't replace: listening, patience, forgiveness, showing up for one another when there's nothing to fix.A personal reflect
picks.reason: Rabbi Yoshi links ancient Jewish texts to modern ethical questions about AI.

picks.title: Chullin 141 and 142 - The End
picks.summary:
On today’s pages, Chullin 141 and 142, we reach the end of Tractate Chullin and look back at what months of studying meat, kashrut, and the intricacies of eating have taught us. Rabbi Dovid Bashevkin joins us to explain why our most basic need for nourishment can become an expression of Jewish identity—and a reminder that we depend on something beyond ourselves. What does keeping kosher ultimately ask us to sanctify? Listen and find out.



Also, celebrate the end of Tractate Chullin with Chullin out, our playlist of every song we referenced along the way.
